research_question: Does the current typed-change-channel selective recompilation core preserve full-rebuild equivalence without stale carry-over on a fresh, pre-registered set of real public document revisions, and what rebuild fraction does it achieve?
selection_rule: Titles were fixed before any corpus fetch for this experiment and exclude every title used by the earlier local H1-B/H1-F public-revision work known at preparation time.

projection.unit: eligible MediaWiki section with normalized body length >= 120 characters
projection.identity: title + canonical heading path, with the live current-core logical identity resolver allowed to abstain
projection.document_shape: heading paths + block count + unit order
projection.artifacts: one section artifact per logical unit + one document index + deterministic four-bucket topic projections

claim_boundary: Fresh prospective public-revision evidence for the current typed-change-channel Core on a deterministic Wikipedia section projection. It is not evidence of OCR quality, domain-specific legal/regulatory correctness, ontology quality, or production customer-data performance.
